title: Whole application
summary: Prepare trusted knowledge ahead of time; retrieve permitted evidence and assemble context at runtime. The model lifecycle and four supporting pillars help coordinate, protect, evaluate, and monitor both flows.
constraint: Locate the failed responsibility, then state the requirement the solution must satisfy.
managed: Use managed model, data, orchestration, and control capabilities where their contracts fit.
extension: Look for a supported extension at the specific layer before replacing its pipeline.
ownership: Own the unsupported gap, including its recovery, authorization, evaluation, and operations.
capability: Choose a layer first. AWS services implement responsibilities; they are not the architecture itself.
clue: Ask: where is the problem → what is the constraint → what is managed → is an extension supported → what must I own?
trap: A custom requirement at one stage does not justify rebuilding the whole application.

title: Source
summary: Approved facts, media, and datasets enter here. Establish provenance, versions, permitted use, and update/delete behavior before creating derived copies.
constraint: Input modality, freshness, permission, and authoritative source version.
managed: S3/object storage, databases, and supported data connectors provide source access and storage.
extension: Pre-extract or adapt unsupported source formats/connectors while preserving provenance.
ownership: Own unsupported connectors and source validation; carry source/version/ACL metadata into derived evidence.
capability: Amazon S3, supported database/connectors, and authoritative business APIs.
clue: “Private manuals change daily” points to current source evidence and synchronization, not memorizing facts in weights.
trap: Changing a source object does not prove the index, cache, or generated answer was refreshed.

title: Preprocess
summary: Convert or validate inputs before creating chunks, embeddings, datasets, or model requests. Preserve meaning rather than merely producing text.
constraint: Document structure, modality, schema quality, sensitive spans, and approved downstream format.
managed: Supported extraction, transcription, ETL, and text-analysis capabilities perform bounded transformations.
extension: Add validation, reconstruction, or verified redaction around supported outputs.
ownership: Own domain-specific transformations and unsupported formats; quarantine failures before indexing or logging.
capability: Textract, Transcribe, Glue/Data Quality, Comprehend, or supported Bedrock Data Automation.
clue: “The PDF condition disappeared during extraction” is a parsing/preprocessing problem before retrieval.
trap: Detection is not redaction, and accurate embeddings cannot restore missing extracted text.

title: Ingestion
summary: Build searchable evidence: Parse → Chunk → Metadata → Embed → Index. This is preparation/synchronization work, not the per-question ranking path.
constraint: Preserve source meaning, useful evidence units, metadata, vector compatibility, and freshness.
managed: Bedrock Knowledge Bases orchestrates supported ingestion, embedding, indexing, and source synchronization.
extension: Knowledge Bases Lambda transformation supports custom chunking and chunk metadata under its contract.
ownership: Own only unsupported ingestion behavior; a compatible extension can leave the remaining pipeline managed.
capability: Bedrock Knowledge Bases ingestion with supported parsers, chunking, embedding model, and vector store.
clue: “Custom chunk boundaries, managed retrieval retained” points to an ingestion extension.
trap: A Lambda ingestion transformation does not control query-time ranking.

title: Knowledge store
summary: Keep searchable chunks, vectors, metadata, and source references. A Knowledge Base coordinates RAG; its vector store holds/searches the indexed evidence.
constraint: Supported query/storage features, metadata filtering, scale, synchronization, and access boundaries.
managed: Knowledge Bases integrates supported stores and offers managed retrieval/generation APIs.
extension: Configure supported stores, metadata, retrieval options, and application-side context processing.
ownership: Own custom retrieval only where the managed path lacks required behavior. Assess support before deciding.
capability: Bedrock Knowledge Bases with OpenSearch or another supported vector store.
clue: “OpenSearch is the backing store” does not say who owns the rest of RAG.
trap: OpenSearch does not automatically mean custom RAG. A vector database is not an enterprise assistant.

title: User / API
summary: Accept a request with trusted identity, its task, and an appropriate delivery contract. Carry scope and correlation through downstream stages.
constraint: Authenticated caller, tenant entitlement, request limits, private access, and interactive versus background completion.
managed: API Gateway, identity/federation services, and eligible private service endpoints supply entry-point capabilities.
extension: Application validation/router logic can enforce team entitlement, token admission, and model routes.
ownership: Own business/data authorization and request policy that generic API throttles cannot express.
capability: API Gateway + application adapter/router; Cognito or federation where appropriate.
clue: “Several teams need common model policy” points to a shared gateway, not just direct invocation.
trap: Authentication identifies the caller; it does not establish document or tool entitlement.

title: Retrieval
summary: Turn a question into permitted candidates, rank them, and select evidence for context. Query → query embedding → vector/lexical/hybrid → candidates → reranker → best context.
constraint: Evidence coverage, exact identifiers, access filters, ranking, and context budget.
managed: Knowledge Bases Retrieve/RetrieveAndGenerate and supported store/search/reranking options cover configured retrieval behavior.
extension: Compose supported retrieval calls, filters, reranking, or context selection when the combined path is insufficient.
ownership: Own unsupported query/ranking policy at this layer, retaining managed ingestion where it still fits.
capability: Knowledge Bases, supported OpenSearch lexical/vector/hybrid search, and supported Bedrock reranking.
clue: Absent candidate → retrieval/earlier evidence boundary. Present but poorly ordered → reranking.
trap: Reranking cannot recover material absent from its candidate input.

title: Prompt / context
summary: System instructions + prompt template + user query + retrieved knowledge + conversation context become the model input. Keep untrusted data separate from governing instructions.
constraint: Clear task/rules, correct evidence, relevant conversation state, context size, and output contract.
managed: Bedrock Prompt Management supplies reusable supported templates/configuration and versions; inference APIs accept context/messages.
extension: Application context assembly supplies permitted evidence/history and supported structured-output configuration.
ownership: Own evidence selection, authoritative state, prompt release gates, and semantic/business validation.
capability: Prompt Management; Converse/ConverseStream or model-specific APIs with application-managed context.
clue: “Right evidence, wrong answer” requires inspecting actual context and task instructions before assuming retrieval is broken.
trap: A versioned prompt, valid JSON, or low temperature does not establish factual truth.

title: Model
summary: Invoke a compatible evaluated model using permitted context. Choose the hosting boundary by required controls, not by whether something is “custom.”
constraint: Model capability, customization support, latency/capacity, serving control, and approved processing Regions.
managed: Bedrock abstracts eligible FM inference infrastructure; SageMaker AI offers managed ML training/hosting services with deeper controls.
extension: Bedrock supports eligible customization/import; SageMaker supports compatible model/serving implementations.
ownership: Take container/GPU/endpoint control when required, and accept its capacity/deployment responsibilities.
capability: Amazon Bedrock for managed FM-centric integration; SageMaker AI when deeper ML/hosting control is decisive.
clue: “Choose GPU family and serving container” points to hosting control. “Fine-tuned model” alone does not.
trap: Custom does not automatically mean SageMaker. Bedrock also supports eligible customization.

title: Response
summary: Deliver and validate the result under the caller’s contract. An answer, source citation, tool outcome, and durable job completion are different artifacts.
constraint: Complete versus incremental delivery, user waiting, background completion, and verified outcome.
managed: Supported Bedrock synchronous/streaming calls and batch jobs supply model-operation contracts.
extension: A streaming adapter forwards events; asynchronous application workers persist job state/results.
ownership: Own end-to-end transport, safe partial-output handling, job reconciliation, and business outcome validation.
capability: Converse / ConverseStream; asynchronous jobs/workers; supported Bedrock batch inference.
clue: Earlier tokens while the user waits → streaming. Caller can leave → async; offline dataset → eligible batch.
trap: Streaming is not asynchronous. A job acknowledgment is not completed business work.

title: Model lifecycle
summary: Requirements → representative data → Select → optional Customize/train → Evaluate + approve → Deploy/invoke → Monitor → revisit selection or customization. This changes the model configuration used at runtime; it is not repeated for each request. Prompt engineering and RAG change runtime instructions/evidence rather than model weights.
constraint: Task/model fit, data quality, measured benefit, release safety, reproducibility, and rollback.
managed: Bedrock provides supported model/customization/evaluation operations; SageMaker supplies broader ML lifecycle capabilities.
extension: Version approved datasets and compatible model artifacts; add calibrated evaluations and approval gates.
ownership: Own release criteria, custom training/serving needs, human accountability, and rollback verification.
capability: Bedrock capabilities and/or SageMaker AI pipelines, training, governed artifacts, and endpoints according to the controls needed.
clue: Compare the selected or customized model against a held-out baseline; use monitoring evidence to revisit selection or customization.
trap: A trained model or registered artifact is not proof of a safe, deployed, working release.

title: Orchestration
summary: Choose who controls progress across either data or runtime work: bounded code, explicit states, decoupled events, or model-selected actions.
constraint: Who chooses the next step? Duration, durability, waits, retries, approval, and coupling.
managed: Lambda executes bounded tasks; Step Functions persists explicit workflows; EventBridge routes events; SQS buffers work.
extension: Bounded model/tool calls can be composed into workflows; persistent compatible tool services can use ECS/Fargate.
ownership: Own action authority, idempotency, rate control, and unsupported runtime/coordination logic.
capability: Lambda | Step Functions | EventBridge / SQS | Bedrock Agents or an appropriate agent framework.
clue: Known durable sequence + wait/approval → Step Functions. Model chooses next tool from observations → agent.
trap: An agent framework does not replace durable workflow state or business authorization.

title: Security / governance
summary: Apply identity, access, isolation, encryption, network, safety, PII, and governance controls at the boundaries they protect—not as one final filter.
constraint: Caller/data/tool entitlement, sensitive copies, private paths, allowed Regions, retention, and content risk.
managed: IAM/KMS, identity services, supported private endpoints, Guardrails, and data discovery/analysis supply distinct controls.
extension: Application authorization/filtering, validation, redaction, and release/governance checks enforce workload-specific policy.
ownership: Own tenant scope before context, transaction rules before writes, derived-copy handling, and unsupported policy checks.
capability: Authentication + IAM/data authorization + isolation + KMS + network policy + appropriate safety/PII controls.
clue: Tenant A must not retrieve tenant B’s documents → access/filtering before context.
trap: Guardrails is not authorization. Private transport or encryption does not establish entitlement or approved residency.

title: Evaluation / diagnosis
summary: Measure evidence coverage, answer/task quality, safety, latency, and cost before releases and during operation. Diagnose backwards using observed boundary evidence.
constraint: Which quality failed, which cohort failed, and at what architecture boundary?
managed: Supported Bedrock model/RAG evaluations supply automated/judge/human approaches; metrics/traces support operational evidence.
extension: Add calibrated rubrics, expert labels, deterministic assertions, tool-outcome tests, and cohort gates.
ownership: Own representative held-out datasets, metric interpretation, judge calibration, and release/rollback policy.
capability: Recall/precision, faithfulness/correctness/relevance, safety, task success, first-token/total latency, and cost per successful outcome.
clue: Missing evidence, noisy retrieval, and unsupported generated claims are different defects.
trap: High average quality, a real citation, or low latency can hide a critical cohort or unsafe side effect.

title: Observability
summary: Collect the evidence needed for the question: trends, caller activity, interaction content, or time across request stages.
constraint: What happened, to which request/version/caller, at which stage—and what can be safely retained?
managed: CloudWatch metrics/logs, CloudTrail events, supported invocation logging, and tracing capture different evidence.
extension: Instrument spans and custom quality signals; correlate IDs and version attribution across application/model/tool stages.
ownership: Own missing instrumentation, sanitized content policy, retention, delivery monitoring, and investigation queries.
capability: CloudWatch | CloudTrail | Bedrock Model Invocation Logging | X-Ray / OpenTelemetry | agent/tool traces.
clue: Who called → CloudTrail. Prompt/response → invocation logging. Trend → metrics. Slow stage → spans.
trap: Enabling Lambda tracing does not expose every uninstrumented SDK hop or hidden model internal.

title: Documents / images
summary: S3 manuals, PDFs, scans, and images need source/version identity and a supported parsing or native multimodal path.
clue: Tables and scanned conditions must survive extraction.
trap: A readable text file can still omit a material column or exception.

title: Databases / business records
summary: Query current authoritative records through an authorized supported connector or business API.
clue: Refund status is a live transaction fact, not a generic prompt example.
trap: A correct source connection is not permission for every caller to every row.

title: Audio / media
summary: Use supported native modalities or prepare transcripts/structured output for the chosen downstream path.
clue: Choose the representation the selected model and retrieval path actually support.
trap: Transcription is not compulsory for every supported audio-capable model.

title: Documents / tables → Textract
summary: Extract supported text, forms, and tables; reconstruct and validate relationships against the source.
clue: Condition missing from extracted table → repair extraction before re-indexing.
trap: Larger embeddings or chunks cannot restore a condition never extracted.
capability: Amazon Textract; supported advanced parsing / Bedrock Data Automation where the contract fits.

title: Speech → Transcribe
summary: Prepare supported recordings as text when the downstream pipeline needs transcripts.
clue: Preserve speaker turns and source references when they matter.
trap: Speaker labels do not verify business roles.
capability: Amazon Transcribe, or a supported native audio/model path.

title: ETL / quality → Glue
summary: Normalize approved formats, catalog data, and evaluate explicit schema/data rules before creating derived copies.
clue: Invalid dataset records must fail or be quarantined before training/indexing.
trap: A data-quality report is not automatically a deployment or ingestion gate.
capability: AWS Glue / Glue Data Quality plus explicit pipeline gating.

title: Text / PII → Comprehend
summary: Locate supported entities or sensitive spans; apply and verify required redaction before indexing or logging.
clue: Text-processing PII detection is a different boundary from S3 corpus discovery.
trap: Detection does not itself sanitize every downstream copy.
capability: Amazon Comprehend plus verified application transformation.

title: Parse
summary: Preserve headings, tables, qualifiers, identifiers, and source versions in the extracted evidence.
clue: The condition is absent before chunking → fix parsing.
trap: Do not diagnose chunking when the original meaning was already lost.
constraint: Correct source meaning and structure reach the chunker.

title: Chunking
summary: Create evidence units that balance focused matching, sufficient context, and token budget.
clue: Small matching passage needs surrounding section → evaluate parent/child context.
trap: Semantic or larger chunks are not universally better.
constraint: Preserve meaning while meeting retrieval quality and context-budget targets.

title: Default
summary: Use the service’s default sentence-aware text splitting where representative retrieval tests show it fits.
clue: Start simple when no measured boundary problem requires another strategy.
trap: Default is not proof that table relationships or conditions survived.
capability: Bedrock Knowledge Bases default text chunking.

title: Fixed
summary: Choose explicit token size/overlap to control predictable evidence units.
clue: A condition split across boundaries may need overlap or another context strategy.
trap: More overlap increases indexed material; larger chunks can add noise.
capability: Supported fixed-size Knowledge Bases chunking.

title: Semantic
summary: Split supported text around meaning/topic changes; evaluate the resulting boundaries and additional cost.
clue: Meaning boundaries may help a corpus with topic transitions.
trap: Semantic chunking does not automatically provide parent substitution.
capability: Supported Knowledge Bases semantic chunking.

title: Hierarchical
summary: Match child chunks and return broader parent context when the selected store/configuration supports it.
clue: Focused child match needs surrounding section conditions.
trap: Parent context costs tokens and may reduce the returned result count.
capability: Supported Knowledge Bases hierarchical chunking.

title: Custom
summary: Define domain-specific evidence boundaries when supported built-in strategies do not fit.
clue: Custom chunking does not automatically require custom retrieval.
trap: Check an extension contract before rebuilding ingestion.
extension: Knowledge Bases custom transformation can supply chunking logic.

title: Lambda Transformation
summary: A supported Knowledge Bases ingestion hook supplies custom chunks or chunk-level metadata, then returns output for managed processing.
clue: Custom chunking / chunk metadata → supported ingestion extension.
trap: This hook does not own query-time retrieval or reranking.
managed: Knowledge Bases retains supported embedding/indexing/retrieval responsibilities around the transformation.
extension: Use the prescribed Lambda and intermediate-S3 contract; custom chunking uses the appropriate no-chunking configuration.
ownership: Own and validate the transformation implementation, not the entire RAG pipeline.
capability: Bedrock Knowledge Bases custom transformation with AWS Lambda.

title: Metadata
summary: Attach source/version references, searchable identifiers, and trusted access metadata to evidence.
clue: Tenant filtering and freshness checks depend on reliable metadata.
trap: User-supplied tenant text is not trusted authorization scope.
constraint: Useful, consistent metadata survives indexing and retrieval.

title: Embedding
summary: Represent documents and queries in a compatible embedding space. Smaller vectors can reduce storage, but require retrieval-quality evaluation.
clue: Document vector and query vector must have matching dimensions and compatible model/configuration.
trap: More dimensions do not guarantee accuracy; matching size alone is not sufficient.
constraint: Compatible vectors and measured recall within storage/latency goals.
managed: Supported Bedrock embedding models generate vectors; the vector store performs similarity search.
extension: Select supported dimensions/configuration and rebuild affected vectors consistently.
ownership: Own evaluation and migration consistency when changing embedding model or dimension.
capability: Titan Text Embeddings V2 or another supported embedding model.

title: Titan Text Embeddings V2
summary: Supported vector sizes are 256, 512, and 1,024 dimensions. Compare configurations on the same representative query set.
clue: Keep document/query contracts compatible through an index migration.
trap: Titan G1’s 1,536 dimensions are a different model contract.
capability: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2: 256D / 512D / 1024D.

title: 256D
summary: 256-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.

title: 512D
summary: 512-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.

title: 1024D
summary: 1024-dimensional V2 vectors are a supported configuration. Use compatible query vectors and measure recall, storage, and latency.
clue: Choose based on a measured quality target, not vector size alone.
trap: An index accepting the vector does not prove it meets retrieval recall.

title: Document ↔ query compatibility
summary: Document: 512D ↔ Query: 512D is dimension-compatible. Document: 1024D ↔ Query: 256D is not. Also preserve compatible model/configuration.
clue: A query-only dimension change against the old index breaks the vector contract.
trap: Do not mix embedding spaces just because both vectors have the same length.

title: Index / synchronize
summary: Persist chunks, vectors, metadata, and source versions. Check completed updates/deletes and derived copies.
clue: Source changed but old version retrieved → inspect ingestion/index freshness.
trap: S3 modification alone does not prove a successful index update.
constraint: The intended current approved evidence is actually indexed and searchable.

title: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
summary: Managed RAG coordinates supported source ingestion and retrieval with a supported backing store. Retrieve tests evidence separately; RetrieveAndGenerate combines the configured path.
clue: A managed extension can leave the rest of RAG managed.
trap: Knowledge Bases and its vector store are different responsibilities.

title: OpenSearch / vector stores
summary: Store/search indexed vectors, text, and metadata under the selected integration contract.
clue: A managed Knowledge Base can use OpenSearch as its backing store.
trap: Naming OpenSearch does not imply a fully custom RAG pipeline.
capability: Supported OpenSearch/vector-store integration; verify store and search feature support.

title: Query
summary: Preserve intent, literal identifiers, and trusted scope when forming the retrieval request.
clue: An equipment ID is not interchangeable with semantically similar products.
trap: Normalizing away meaningful identifiers can destroy exact matching.

title: Query embedding
summary: Generate the query representation compatible with indexed document vectors.
clue: Document/query dimensions and model space must remain compatible.
trap: Changing the query model alone does not migrate the document index.
capability: The compatible embedding model/configuration used by the indexed corpus.

title: Vector / semantic
summary: Find candidates by semantic similarity in a compatible vector space.
clue: Meaning similarity helps paraphrases and concept queries.
trap: Similar text is not proof of exact identifier match or permission.
capability: Supported vector retrieval through Knowledge Bases / the selected store.

title: BM25 / lexical
summary: Use literal terms and identifiers as retrieval signals; field configuration and tokenization still matter.
clue: AX-1047 / SKU / policy code may need lexical matching or an exact field lookup.
trap: A semantic similarity score alone can miss a literal identifier.
capability: OpenSearch lexical/BM25 or exact identifier lookup where configured.

title: Hybrid
summary: Combine semantic and lexical signals where the selected store/API supports it, then evaluate candidate coverage and relevance.
clue: The question contains both an exact asset ID and a semantic symptom.
trap: Hybrid support and quality vary; it is not universally the best search.
capability: Supported hybrid retrieval configuration, for example eligible OpenSearch-backed paths.

title: Candidates
summary: Inspect the permitted evidence actually returned before reranking. Missing candidates may reflect indexing, freshness, filters, or query behavior.
clue: Indexed and authorized source missing here → evaluate candidate recall and query/search.
trap: A reranker cannot score a document absent from its input.
constraint: The required permitted evidence enters the candidate set.

title: Reranker
summary: Reorder existing candidates for relevance to the question before pruning context. This adds a ranking stage, not a new source-ingestion path.
clue: Correct passage is present but placed below irrelevant candidates.
trap: Reranking cannot restore text never parsed/indexed/retrieved.
constraint: The needed evidence is present but its ordering/selection is poor.
managed: Supported Bedrock reranker models score supplied query/document candidates.
extension: Use supported reranking configuration or compose a reranking call over collected candidates.
ownership: Own unsupported ranking policy and its latency/cost evaluation, not unrelated ingestion.
capability: Supported Bedrock reranking / ranking configuration.

title: Best context
summary: Select authorized relevant evidence within the context budget, preserving qualifications and source references.
clue: Good candidate can still be lost by pruning or truncation before generation.
trap: Top-ranked alone does not mean complete, permitted, or source-supported.

title: System instructions
summary: State task authority, behavior, boundaries, and insufficient-information handling.
clue: Separate governing instructions from untrusted source passages.
trap: A system instruction is not a deterministic access-control boundary.

title: Prompt template
summary: Version reusable task instructions, variables, and supported model configuration.
clue: Reproducible prompt releases → Prompt Management.
trap: Saving a version does not mean it passed evaluation.
capability: Bedrock Prompt Management plus application release/evaluation gates.

title: User query
summary: Define the requested task clearly and preserve the question the evidence should answer.
clue: Different label definitions or overlap policies create different classification tasks.
trap: A persona cannot fill in an undefined decision rule.

title: Retrieved knowledge
summary: Supply selected permitted passages as evidence, keeping their identifiers and source conditions.
clue: A cited passage must actually support the answer claim.
trap: Treat document instructions as untrusted data rather than system authority.

title: Conversation context
summary: Supply relevant permitted history and authoritative state explicitly; trim within the context budget.
clue: Converse accepts messages; the application owns the history it sends.
trap: An inference call is not automatically a persistent conversation store.

title: Amazon Bedrock
summary: Use eligible managed foundation models, inference APIs, customization, and supporting GenAI capabilities without choosing endpoint GPU fleets.
clue: Managed FM-centric application integration fits without infrastructure selection.
trap: Bedrock supports eligible customization; “custom weights” alone does not require SageMaker.
capability: Bedrock inference/customization/import features where supported.

title: SageMaker AI
summary: Choose deeper ML training, serving-container, instance, endpoint, and lifecycle controls where they are decisive.
clue: GPU family + serving container + endpoint autoscaling requirements.
trap: More control adds ownership; do not choose it merely because a prompt or chunker is custom.
managed: SageMaker provides managed ML services while exposing supported training/hosting configuration.
ownership: Own the model/container configuration, compatible artifacts, deployment, capacity, and validation.
capability: SageMaker AI training and eligible hosted endpoint configurations.

title: Synchronous
summary: The caller waits for one complete bounded response.
clue: Short complete answer needed before proceeding.
trap: A larger timeout does not turn the path into durable background work.
capability: Supported Converse / InvokeModel and a bounded request path.

title: Streaming / ConverseStream
summary: Expose incremental generated output while the caller stays connected; every transport hop must preserve streaming.
clue: Need earlier visible tokens while the user waits.
trap: Streaming does not imply background completion or lower total inference cost.
capability: ConverseStream / InvokeModelWithResponseStream with an eligible streaming transport.

title: Asynchronous
summary: Return durable acceptance/job identity and finish later with persisted status/results and failure handling.
clue: Caller can leave; accepted work must survive transient worker failures.
trap: Acknowledged is not completed, and a queue does not by itself enforce token rate.
capability: SQS + paced Lambda/container workers + durable results; event/workflow patterns where appropriate.

title: Batch
summary: Process a supported offline dataset as a managed inference job and reconcile record-level results.
clue: Many offline requests; no immediate live answer is needed.
trap: Batch support, input format, economics, and completion semantics depend on the model/Region contract.
capability: Supported Bedrock batch inference over an approved S3 dataset.

title: Select
summary: Compare supported model capability, modalities, context limits, quality, safety, latency, cost, and deployment requirements.
clue: Choose with representative tasks and a held-out baseline.
trap: A public benchmark rank does not establish fit for this workload.

title: Choose context or model changes
summary: Change instructions, evidence, or weights according to the observed deficiency; these approaches can combine. Prompt → RAG → weights: escalate only for an unmet need. This is an application decision, separate from the model-only lifecycle.
clue: Missing current facts differs from unstable instructions or stable style needs. Change instructions, evidence, or weights deliberately; evaluate each against a held-out baseline.
trap: RAG is not fine-tuning and neither is required for every model change.
extension: Version prompts, retrieval, datasets, tools, and supported model artifacts; add calibrated evaluations and approval gates.

title: Model customization / training (optional)
summary: Change the model only for an evaluated need. Fine-tuning uses suitable labeled data; continued pre-training uses suitable unlabeled domain text where supported; distillation trains an eligible smaller student from teacher-generated behavior. LoRA is a fine-tuning technique, not a separate source of knowledge. An unchanged selected model can proceed to evaluation.
constraint: A measured stable behavior, domain adaptation, or serving quality/cost need; suitable data and a supported model/workflow.
managed: Bedrock provides supported model/customization/evaluation operations; SageMaker supplies broader ML lifecycle capabilities.
extension: Eligible Bedrock model customization or SageMaker training according to support/control needs.
ownership: Own release criteria, custom training/serving needs, human accountability, and rollback verification.
capability: Eligible Bedrock model customization or SageMaker training according to support/control needs.
clue: Stable behavior → fine-tuning; supported domain-text adaptation → continued pre-training; smaller student → distillation.
trap: RAG is not fine-tuning and neither is required for every model change.

title: Prompt engineering
summary: Clarify task, decision rules, examples, and supported output constraints before adding weight changes.
clue: Policy ambiguity or a missing few-shot boundary.
trap: A valid schema or low temperature cannot supply a missing fact.
capability: Versioned prompts, Prompt Management, supported schema controls, and evaluation.

title: RAG
summary: Retrieve current private evidence into context rather than relying on model weights to track updates.
clue: Frequently changing source facts with attribution.
trap: RAG still needs ingestion freshness, authorization, retrieval quality, and faithful context use.
capability: Knowledge Bases or a justified composed/custom retrieval layer.

title: Fine-tuning
summary: Use suitable labeled training data for an evaluated stable behavior/task need when supported prompting is insufficient.
clue: Consistent domain behavior with a demonstrated quality gain.
trap: Daily private-document refresh and citations are not implemented merely by changing weights.
capability: Eligible Bedrock model customization or SageMaker training according to support/control needs.

title: Continued pre-training
summary: Adapt eligible models on suitable unlabeled domain text where the model/feature supports it; evaluate against the original baseline.
clue: Domain adaptation differs from supervised instruction examples.
trap: This option is model-specific and not a real-time source lookup.
capability: Supported continued pre-training or an appropriate controlled training workflow.

title: Datasets / splits
summary: Version approved training/tuning data and separate representative held-out evaluation data with source/tool references.
clue: Preserve expert labels and rare/critical cohorts.
trap: Tuning on the held-out final test invalidates its independence.

title: Evaluate / human gates
summary: Measure quality, correctness, faithfulness, safety, latency, and cost; use calibrated automated/judge checks and accountable human review where needed.
clue: Critical regression blocks promotion even when averages improve.
trap: Human review and automated evaluation complement each other; neither is automatically infallible.
capability: Supported Bedrock evaluations, deterministic checks, expert review, and approval workflows.

title: Deploy / invoke
summary: Release a compatible approved model/prompt/retrieval configuration with version attribution and rollback.
clue: Control serving infrastructure only when required.
trap: A registered artifact does not automatically update an endpoint.

title: Capacity / routing
summary: Separate intermittent on-demand use, measured reserved capacity, and eligible cross-Region routing.
clue: Stable demand and approved processing destinations are different constraints.
trap: An inference profile does not independently fail over the source application or provide chosen GPU controls.
capability: Eligible on-demand / Provisioned Throughput / inference profiles; SageMaker endpoint capacity where required.

title: Monitor / improve
summary: Correlate production versions and outcomes, turn failures into regressions, and roll back critical degradation.
clue: Quality drift and failed tool outcomes need more than uptime metrics.
trap: A monitoring chart does not itself generate calibrated quality scores.

title: One bounded task → Lambda
summary: Run a bounded operation and externalize durable state. Split long waits into an appropriate workflow/job.
clue: Short stateless adapter, validation, or lookup.
trap: Warm execution memory is not a guaranteed persistent service lifecycle.
capability: AWS Lambda; provisioned concurrency targets initialization, reserved concurrency targets allocation/caps.

title: Known durable workflow → Step Functions
summary: Developers define states, retries, branches, and approval waits. Bounded Bedrock/tool tasks can sit inside the workflow.
clue: Known sequence + durable state + hours-long approval.
trap: Model-selected autonomy is not needed just because a process is complex.
managed: Standard workflows retain execution state and support appropriate callback/recovery patterns.
extension: Invoke bounded tasks and approved integrations under scoped roles.
ownership: Own the explicit state definition, approval identity/deadline, and idempotent external actions.
capability: AWS Step Functions Standard where the durability/integration contract fits.

title: Model chooses next tool → Agent
summary: The model reasons over observations to choose among permitted actions. Bound tools, time, iterations, tokens, and write authority.
clue: The next tool cannot be expressed as a known fixed sequence.
trap: Framework/runtime choice does not supply business authorization.
capability: Bedrock Agents or an appropriate framework such as Strands; eligible runtime/tool hosting as needed.

title: Decouple / buffer → Events / SQS
summary: EventBridge routes events to targets; SQS retains work for paced consumers. These can support ingestion or runtime jobs.
clue: Independent event consumers differ from a worker buffer under a fixed model rate.
trap: Queues do not automatically implement token-rate admission.
capability: EventBridge rules/targets; SQS with bounded/rate-controlled workers, retry/DLQ, and idempotency.

title: Tool runtime / MCP hosting
summary: Match each tool’s duration, dependencies, connection lifecycle, and compute needs. Use a persistent service only when it is required.
clue: Long-lived compatible CPU service differs from a short DynamoDB lookup.
trap: External session state alone does not force every handler into containers.
capability: Lambda for bounded handlers; eligible ECS/Fargate services for persistent CPU runtimes.

title: Authentication / IAM
summary: Identify the caller and evaluate allowed AWS actions/resources using the applicable policies and explicit denies.
clue: Who is calling differs from which customer record they may use.
trap: An ingestion role’s source access is not every end user’s document permission.
capability: Cognito/federation + IAM; application/data authorization for business scope.

title: Tenant isolation / retrieval filtering
summary: Derive scope from trusted identity; enforce permitted document access before context and business access before tool writes.
clue: Tenant A must never receive tenant B’s passages.
trap: A high similarity score or a Guardrail does not grant access.
managed: Supported store/Knowledge Base filters help enforce configured scope; identity APIs establish the caller.
extension: Backend ACL checks and trusted metadata filters bind retrieval to caller entitlement.
ownership: Own caller-to-document mapping, fail-closed metadata handling, and bypass-path tests.
capability: IAM plus application/data authorization and supported retrieval filters.

title: KMS / encryption
summary: Protect source, intermediate, vector, result, state, and log copies with required encryption and key access.
clue: Inventory derived copies rather than protecting only original S3 objects.
trap: Encryption does not authorize a tenant or prove deletion.
capability: AWS KMS, service encryption configuration, TLS, and controlled key policies.

title: VPC / PrivateLink
summary: Use eligible interface endpoints, private DNS, endpoint policies, and network controls for the required private API path.
clue: API traffic must stay on the approved private path.
trap: A private subnet alone is not a private service endpoint.
capability: Supported VPC endpoints / AWS PrivateLink and configured network/endpoint policies.

title: Guardrails / content safety
summary: Apply supported content, sensitive-information, and grounding policies at the interaction stages they cover.
clue: Harmful content and unsupported claims need the appropriate safety check.
trap: Guardrails is not authorization or a guarantee against every indirect/tool-result injection.
capability: Supported Amazon Bedrock Guardrails policies plus deterministic application checks.

title: PII / sensitive copies
summary: Locate where PII exists, choose discovery/detection/filtering for that location, and verify required transformation/retention.
clue: S3 discovery → Macie; supported text pipeline → Comprehend; model interaction → Guardrails.
trap: Detecting sensitive spans does not sanitize every index, log, or backup.
capability: Macie / Comprehend / Guardrails at their respective boundaries.

title: Permission ceilings / residency / retention
summary: Use applicable organizational/identity ceilings and approved processing destinations; manage retention and deletion of derived copies.
clue: Local IAM allow cannot override an applicable explicit SCP deny.
trap: Permission ceilings do not grant access; private encrypted transport does not establish residency.
capability: SCPs / permissions boundaries, supported endpoint/profile policy, configuration/audit controls.

title: Recall / precision
summary: Recall assesses required-evidence coverage; precision/relevance assesses retrieval noise. Inspect actual candidates/context as well as scores.
clue: Missing relevant passage differs from too many irrelevant passages.
trap: Good retrieval does not guarantee faithful generation.

title: Correctness / faithfulness / relevance
summary: Correctness compares with references, faithfulness checks source support, and relevance checks whether the response answers the question.
clue: Correct evidence with an unsupported claim → faithfulness/context-use investigation.
trap: A real citation or valid JSON does not prove source support.

title: Automated / judge / human
summary: Use deterministic checks for objective contracts, calibrated judges for semantic scale, and experts for labels/high-risk nuance.
clue: Thousands of rubric-scored answers with a limited expert sample → calibrated judge plus targeted human review.
trap: BLEU/ROUGE overlap is not semantic truth; judge scores can be biased or wrong.

title: Safety / latency / cost
summary: Assess critical cohorts, actual tool outcomes, first-token/total/queue latency, and tokens/cost per successful outcome.
clue: Faster first text differs from lower total generation time.
trap: The cheapest invocation can be expensive per successful task if it fails or retries.

title: Repeated work / caching
summary: Identify the reusable unit: exact scoped result, semantically equivalent answer, or supported identical prompt prefix.
clue: Stable system prefix with new answers → prompt caching.
trap: A prompt cache is not response reuse; response cache keys must include scope and version.
capability: Eligible Bedrock prompt caching; scoped application result caches where valid.

title: Release / rollout
summary: Offline gates precede controlled exposure. Canary limits live exposure; A/B compares live outcomes; shadow compares isolated copied requests.
clue: Candidate output must not reach users and writes must not occur → isolated shadow.
trap: Hiding the candidate answer does not suppress production tool side effects.

title: Review / diagnose
summary: Review a whole path forward to understand its responsibilities. Choose an observed symptom to investigate backwards through earlier boundaries.
clue: Find the first demonstrated inconsistency using versioned inputs, metrics, traces, and actual outputs.
trap: Do not debug training loss for a routing defect, rerank an absent chunk, or use Guardrails as tenant authorization.

title: CloudWatch metrics / alarms
summary: Track token counts, latency distributions, throttles/errors, queue age, and emitted quality/outcome signals.
clue: Operational threshold on InputTokenCount → metric alarm.
trap: Cost Explorer analyzes billing and Budgets alerts; neither is this runtime metric alarm.
capability: CloudWatch metrics/alarms; configured custom application signals.

title: CloudTrail caller audit
summary: Record required AWS API activity with the appropriate event coverage; correlate caller, time, and operation.
clue: Who invoked or changed an AWS resource?
trap: Caller audit events are not the complete model input/output record.
capability: AWS CloudTrail with required event coverage/selectors.

title: Invocation / application logging
summary: Explicitly enable supported interaction-content logging where policy allows; protect destinations, retention, and sensitive inputs.
clue: Need the actual prompt and answer rather than only the caller.
trap: Logging is not enabled by assuming CloudTrail; logs can retain sensitive pre-masking input.
capability: Bedrock Model Invocation Logging to protected CloudWatch Logs / S3, plus scoped application/tool logs.

title: Spans / agent / tool traces
summary: Instrument retrieval, model, and tool boundaries; retain relevant workflow/agent events and correlate them with request/version identity.
clue: Which stage consumed eight seconds or caused the tool failure?
trap: Uninstrumented stages and hidden model internals do not automatically become visible.
capability: X-Ray / OpenTelemetry, emitted agent traces, tool logs, and workflow history.

title: Training records / task format
summary: Validate model-specific schemas, input/output alignment, labels, duplicate examples, and cohort coverage before a training job.
clue: Clean task examples matter more than raw record count.
trap: A successful schema check does not prove label correctness or prevent data leakage.
capability: Approved S3 datasets; Glue quality/preparation and model-specific validation.

title: Training configuration
summary: Verify the supported base model/method, tokenizer and sequence format, learning rate, epochs, batch configuration, and available compute.
clue: Loss diverges after a learning-rate change → inspect the training configuration and data.
trap: More epochs or a higher learning rate is not a universal fix.
capability: Eligible Bedrock customization settings or SageMaker training configuration.

title: Training / validation curves
summary: Compare available training and validation metrics over time, plus held-out task outputs; retain the job, dataset, configuration, and checkpoint versions.
clue: Training improves while held-out behavior worsens → investigate generalization, leakage, and overfitting.
trap: Low training loss is not proof of useful or safe production behavior.
capability: Bedrock customization output metrics where available; SageMaker training logs/metrics.

title: Checkpoint / generalization
summary: Choose an artifact using independent task evaluation and critical-cohort gates, not merely the final epoch or lowest training loss.
clue: Original model beats the tuned candidate on held-out tasks → stop promotion and inspect the adaptation/data.
trap: A final training checkpoint is not automatically the best release.

title: LoRA / parameter-efficient tuning
summary: Train low-rank adapter weights while the base weights remain frozen. An unmerged adapter still needs its compatible base model at inference.
clue: Task adaptation with a smaller trainable artifact → evaluate supported LoRA.
trap: LoRA is a fine-tuning technique, not RAG, a standalone foundation model, or a guarantee of higher quality.
managed: Eligible SageMaker customization and compatible serving capabilities support adapter workflows; check the selected model/runtime contract.
extension: Use supported adapter training and serving integration rather than assuming arbitrary hot-swapping.
ownership: Version and evaluate the adapter together with its base model, tokenizer, and serving configuration.
capability: Supported LoRA training; compatible SageMaker adapter inference components where applicable.

title: Rank / scaling / dropout
summary: Rank changes adapter capacity and resource use; scaling and dropout alter the training behavior. Tune with representative validation rather than a universal setting.
clue: Insufficient adaptation capacity differs from memorization or bad labels.
trap: Increasing rank does not repair wrong supervision and does not always improve generalization.

title: Adapter / base compatibility
summary: Track the exact base revision, adapter artifact, tokenizer/template, and supported serving format together. Check whether the adapter is merged or separately loaded.
clue: Small adapter file exists, but the request behaves like the base → check loading and routing.
trap: An adapter is not a complete model; matching a model-family name alone is insufficient.

title: Version / approval / Model Registry
summary: Record approved versioned artifacts, metrics, lineage, and rollback targets. Keep approval separate from the explicit deployment action.
clue: Approved model package, unchanged live output → inspect endpoint deployment and request routing.
trap: Model Registry approval does not update an endpoint or load a LoRA adapter.
capability: SageMaker Model Registry plus a governed deployment workflow.

title: LoRA serving / adapter routing
summary: Deploy the compatible base and selected adapter through a supported runtime. Verify the adapter identity actually invoked, loading status, authorization, and version attribution.
clue: Multiple task adapters share a base, but one tenant gets the wrong behavior → inspect adapter routing and access.
trap: Generic endpoint updates, merged-model releases, and adapter inference components have different deployment contracts.
capability: Compatible SageMaker adapter inference components or supported container adapter serving.

title: Verify live release / rollback
summary: Check actual endpoint/component readiness and send a version-attributed smoke request through the real application route. Verify rollback restores a compatible full release.
clue: Offline candidate passes but live behavior is old → inspect deployed identity and route.
trap: Artifact registration or a completed update request is not proof that the intended version serves users.

title: Generation / context configuration
summary: Check actual token limits, stop sequences, sampling configuration, supported API fields, tokenizer/template, and context truncation.
clue: Answer cuts off or differs from evaluation → inspect the actual inference payload/configuration.
trap: Lower temperature does not repair missing knowledge, a wrong adapter, or lost context.

title: Quantization / serving fit
summary: Reduce weight precision where the model/runtime supports it; measure memory, latency, and critical task quality on the target serving configuration.
clue: A memory footprint requirement points to serving/model representation, not chunk size.
trap: Smaller weights are not automatically faster or equally accurate; adapter/runtime compatibility still matters.
capability: Supported model/runtime quantization with measured endpoint benchmarks.

title: Distillation
summary: Train an eligible smaller student from teacher-generated behavior using a supported workflow and representative tasks. Compare held-out quality, latency, and cost.
clue: Reduce serving cost for a defined task while preserving measured quality.
trap: Distillation is different from quantizing the same model or attaching a LoRA adapter.
capability: Eligible Bedrock distillation or a controlled SageMaker training workflow.

title: Token admission / queueing
summary: Inspect accepted request/token volume, queue age, timeouts, quotas, and team scope; pace accepted work against the real model capacity.
clue: 429s or long queue waits under bursts → examine admission and capacity before tuning prompts.
trap: API request throttles, worker concurrency, and billing alerts are not interchangeable token-budget controls.

title: Tool arguments / business validation
summary: Inspect the chosen tool and its parameters, caller scope, preconditions, approvals, and authoritative outcome. Reject invalid writes before execution.
clue: Valid JSON but unauthorized or invalid action → deterministic authorization/business validation.
trap: Schema conformance is not permission or transaction correctness.

title: Retries / idempotency / reconciliation
summary: Correlate retries and duplicate deliveries with durable work identity, execution state, DLQs, and the authoritative business record.
clue: Timeout followed by duplicate payment → inspect idempotency and result reconciliation.
trap: A model response or queue acknowledgment does not prove a side effect completed exactly once.
